result.text:
NEW | Hezbollah’s Limited Options for Supporting Iran by @TheStudyofWar Middle East Researcher Avery Borens

Four Key Takeaways ⬇️

1. Hezbollah’s changed military and political position in Lebanon means that it poses a different threat to Israel from the one it did before the October 7 War, and that any Hezbollah intervention would likely involve a new strategy using new, longer-range, and low-cost weapons.

2. Israel’s 2024 campaign significantly degraded Hezbollah’s capabilities, infrastructure, and forces, depriving Hezbollah of the ability to conduct the kind of military operation it did in 2006, October 2023, or after October 2024.

3. Hezbollah’s weakened position would require Hezbollah to adopt a new strategy in a renewed conflict, likely relying on its long-range weapons and conducting attacks from central and northern Lebanon.

4. The US and Israeli war against Iran, which explicitly seeks to encourage regime change, will likely trigger Hezbollah intervention.

result.text:
Iran war (Day 2)
- The US-Israeli campaign appeared organized initially around suppressing Iranian air defenses, degrading Iranian retaliatory capabilities, and disrupting Iranian command-and-control. More recently, US-Israeli strikes have targeted internal security institutions, which could degrade the regime ability to repress its people.
- Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is confirmed dead, marking the end of the longest-serving autocrat in the world. A leadership council, as prescribed by the Iranian constitution, has emerged to fulfill his duties until a new supreme leader is chosen. Don’t expect the new council to abandon the nuclear program or embrace democratic reform, however. They will continue to fight.
- Iran has sustained its strike campaign across the Middle East. Iran seeks to impose costs on the United States and its partners and compel them to abandon the war. Iranian leaders likely calculate that sustained pressure on regional states will drive them eventually to push Washington for a ceasefire. Most Iranian strikes around the Gulf seem focused on the UAE so far.
- The Axis of Resistance has been almost a complete non-factor to this point. There have been some reports of Iraqi militias launching strikes but nothing substantial yet. That could change rapidly, of course. But we’re probably seeing the consequence of the Axis of Resistance suffering numerous defeats in recent years.
